name: Image Prompt Dialects
description: Guidance for vocabulary-first tag workflows, including models that also accept natural-language descriptions. Each dialect states lookup sources, spelling and model-control evidence. Lookup scope is not a training-corpus claim or a closed vocabulary; exact model and interface evidence controls use.

dialects.name: Illustrious and NoobAI
dialects.description: Tag-workflow guidance for Illustrious and NoobAI checkpoints. Exact releases and derivatives retain their own input capabilities, vocabulary behavior and sampling settings. Illustrious XL v1.0 supports descriptions and tags; NoobAI XL 1.0 documents native tag captions from Danbooru and e621.
dialects.tag_separator: a comma followed by one space
dialects.multi_word_tags: Keep the selected vocabulary's canonical spelling and apply the exact model's evidenced rendering convention. Spaces and underscores must not be assumed interchangeable on every derivative. An intact underscore form can be compared when a shorter overlapping tag creates an observed ambiguity.
dialects.artist_tag_form: Use the bare artist tag when supported by the selected caption convention. Post frequency is a discovery signal, not a minimum admission threshold or a guarantee of learned style.
block_order: figure count and any interaction between figures
subject appearance needed for the selected depiction, ordered by region
dialects.negative_form: Vocabulary candidates that name a necessary failure, in the negative field, with dictionary search completed for the selected scope: worst quality and low quality for the quality floor; text, watermark, signature, logo, and translation request for generation hygiene; bad hands, extra digits, and fewer digits for hand integrity; extra arms and extra legs for limb integrity; multiple views, comic, 2koma, and 4koma for a single picture; monochrome and greyscale for a colour medium; the rating terms above the requested one for a content rating. When no suitable known tag carries a necessary exclusion, assess model-legible phrasing under the exact interface's evidenced grammar. Preserve the exclusion's meaning and scope in the authored rendition; dictionary membership alone does not decide whether it is needed.

basis.statement: Illustrious XL v1.0 supports plain-English descriptions, Danbooru-style tags and mixtures; derivative behavior requires its own evidence.
NoobAI XL 1.0 identifies Danbooru and e621 training with native tag captions. Its caption order starts with count, character, series and artist, then special and general tags.

Consult Danbooru and e621 vocabulary when preparing tag renditions. Prefer a suitable established near-equivalent; use necessary descriptive extensions when it does not preserve the requested meaning. Dictionary scope does not assert model training provenance.

notes: The block order is an authoring baseline. NoobAI caption order and exact checkpoint recommendations may place artist, quality and period terms differently; preserve the selected scene while applying that evidence.
Order relevant subject details from head toward feet where that sequence fits the subject. This ordering neither requires every region to be described nor selects which regions must be visible.
Rating, quality and period controls are candidates with version-specific meaning. A dialect list does not require one token from every category.

The lookup includes e621 for useful established terminology even when an Illustrious derivative has no documented e621 training data. Search evidence and observed model behavior answer different questions.

dialects.name: Anima
dialects.description: Anima guidance for tag and mixed-language renditions. The family uses a Qwen text encoder and Qwen-Image VAE; the exact base, aesthetic, distilled or derived version determines controls and sampling. Danbooru and e621 are both lookup scopes, without asserting e621 training for the base model.
dialects.tag_separator: a comma followed by one space
dialects.multi_word_tags: Spaces rather than underscores, except the score terms, which keep theirs.
dialects.artist_tag_form: Prefix the artist tag with @; the author describes unprefixed effects as weak.
block_order: optional quality, meta, year and safety controls
subject appearance, body, hair, face and outfit
action, camera, scene, lighting and effects
natural-language relationships where they best convey the selected image
dialects.negative_form: Vocabulary candidates that name a necessary failure, in the negative field with spaces in multi-word tags, with dictionary search completed for the selected scope: text, watermark, and signature for generation hygiene; bad hands and extra digits for hand integrity; multiple views and comic for a single picture; monochrome and greyscale for a colour medium; the rating terms above the requested one for a content rating. When no suitable known tag carries a necessary exclusion, assess model-legible phrasing under the exact interface's evidenced grammar. Preserve the exclusion's meaning and scope in the authored rendition; dictionary membership alone does not decide whether it is needed.

basis.statement: The author documents tag, natural-language and mixed prompts; lowercase space-separated tags, Gelbooru spelling where it differs, @ artist prefixes, and variant-specific quality guidance.

Consult Danbooru and e621 vocabulary when preparing tag renditions. Prefer a suitable established near-equivalent; use necessary descriptive extensions when it does not preserve the requested meaning. Dictionary scope does not assert model training provenance.

notes: Anima-Aesthetic guidance advises against score tags in both channels. Base quality groups are alternatives or optional combinations, not one required stack.
Natural language can carry the scene directly or combine with tags; it is not restricted to a final fallback line.
The weight range is an author-selected trial band for a compatible interface, not a universal Anima optimum. Exact model and parser evidence may require a different value.
This dialect supplies guidance only. It does not establish an executable Anima offering.

dialects.name: NovelAI
dialects.description: Provider-specific tag and mixed-language guidance. Resolve the exact model version and anime or furry mode before applying native controls, parser syntax, limits or reference transport.
dialects.tag_separator: a comma followed by one space
dialects.multi_word_tags: Use the selected NovelAI model's native tag suggestions and provider spelling, including renamed tags. Consult public dictionaries for useful candidates without treating either as a complete provider vocabulary.
dialects.artist_tag_form: Use only the artist form evidenced for the selected model and version.
block_order: count, character and series where applicable
scene, action, relationships and appearance in tags or natural language
optional quality and style controls under exact version guidance
dialects.negative_form: Use the active interface's undesired-content field and its native parser. Search necessary negative tag concepts, select suitable established terms and preserve required meaning with descriptive wording when no suitable tag exists.

basis.statement: Native suggestions, optional known tags, ordering and special controls vary by model and dataset mode.
Anime V3 and Furry V3 have different tag vocabularies. V4 and later document natural-language support and dataset modes.

The Anime artstyle guide documents tags for rendering effects and warns that quality or aesthetic tags can impose a competing style. Its examples do not certify arbitrary medium terms or every model version; apply the selected version's guidance and distinguish documented use from observed results.

Consult Danbooru and e621 vocabulary when preparing tag renditions. Prefer a suitable established near-equivalent; use necessary descriptive extensions when it does not preserve the requested meaning. Dictionary scope does not assert model training provenance.

notes: The family name does not choose Anime V3, Furry V3, a Full or Curated release, or a dataset mode. Preserve that exact choice in the active target.
fur dataset is documented for V4 and later; background dataset for V4.5 and later. Furry mode also changes the native suggestions.
masterpiece is documented for V4.5 and later, top aesthetic for V4 and later, and complexity controls for V5. Do not transfer these controls to earlier models.
Danbooru and e621 are supplementary lookup scopes. The provider documentation cited here does not establish them as complete training corpora.

dialects.name: Pony Diffusion V6 XL
dialects.description: Guidance for the author's V6 XL checkpoint, which accepts both natural-language descriptions and tags. This exact revision's native controls do not define all Pony releases or derivatives.
dialects.tag_separator: a comma followed by one space
dialects.multi_word_tags: Preserve native source, score and rating tokens with underscores. Apply evidenced vocabulary spelling to content tags; natural-language scene descriptions are also supported.
dialects.artist_tag_form: The V6 XL author states that artist names were removed from training captions; do not assume bare artist tags have a documented learned role.
block_order: content tags and optional dataset or rating controls
dialects.negative_form: The author does not require a generic negative stack. Select exclusions from the actual image request and observed failure, search their tag vocabulary, and use the active interface's evidenced negative field.

basis.statement: The V6 XL author documents natural-language and tag training, native score/source/rating controls and an optional recommended score prefix.

Consult Danbooru and e621 vocabulary when preparing tag renditions. Prefer a suitable established near-equivalent; use necessary descriptive extensions when it does not preserve the requested meaning. Dictionary scope does not assert model training provenance.

notes: This is guidance only; no executable model or offering follows from it.

Danbooru and e621 lookup complements the author's native controls. The linked card does not identify every tag database; older Pony Derpibooru evidence must not be applied to V6 XL as an exact corpus claim.
Use the active derivative's evidence if it changes quality terms, artists, captions or parser behavior.
